overview: The Medford City Council approved reprogramming $816,182 in surplus bond funds for school facility improvements, advocated for the restoration of MBTA express bus routes, and requested additional funding and staffing for the upcoming general election. The Council also debated in-person meeting health protocols and historic preservation procedures.

items.title: School Improvement Surplus Funds Reprogramming
items.summary: Approved two papers reprogramming $816,182.53 in surplus bond proceeds from past high school projects toward citywide school facility and HVAC improvements.

items.title: Common Victualler License for 7-Eleven
items.summary: Tabled a license petition for 7-Eleven at 133 Main Street because the applicant was not present.

items.title: Historical Commission Annual Reports
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting annual reports from the Historical Commission from 2016 through 2019 following debate regarding demolition delays and local development.

items.title: Condolences and Moment of Silence
items.summary: Approved resolutions extending condolences to the families of Edward Tyrantz and Giovanni Puccio, followed by a moment of silence.

items.title: Recognition of Armstrong Ambulance
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending Armstrong Ambulance personnel for organizing COVID-19 screening for Medford High School families.

items.title: Crime Statistics and Public Safety Summit
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting monthly police crime statistics reports and calling for a public safety summit to address recent break-ins and home invasions.

items.title: MBTA Express Bus Route Restoration
items.summary: Approved a resolution urging the MBTA to reinstate express bus routes 325 and 326 and requesting a ridership study and reduction in Medford's MBTA assessment.

items.title: Election Staffing and Resource Allocation
items.summary: Approved resolutions urging the administration to provide funding, ballot drop boxes, translations, and an election coordinator position for the November general election.

items.title: DCR Guardrail and River Tree Maintenance
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting DCR repair a damaged guardrail on the Route 16 bridge at Auburn Street and clear fallen trees in the Mystic River.

items.title: Andrews School Collection Bins
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the School Department clear and sanitize overflowing collection bins at the Andrews School.

items.title: Green Line Extension District Planning
items.summary: Approved a resolution to hold a Committee of the Whole meeting to create a corridor district plan around the new Ball Square and Medford-Tufts transit stations.

items.title: Council Meeting Public Health Protocols
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting consultation with the Board of Health on meeting health metrics, while referring a motion to mandate masks behind the rail to the Rules Subcommittee.

items.title: Black Lives Matter Banner Legal Opinion Explanation
items.summary: Ruled out of order a repeated resolution seeking an explanation of legal opinions regarding a Black Lives Matter banner on City Hall after learning a response from the mayor is pending.

items.title: Administration COVID-19 Updates
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting periodic administration updates during Council meetings regarding local COVID-19 metrics and policies.

items.title: 16 Foster Court Historic District Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance establishing a single-parcel historic district at 16 Foster Court to a Committee of the Whole.

items.title: Meeting Minutes Approval and Crosswalk Inquiry
items.summary: Approved the July 28, 2020 meeting records, tabled the August 25, 2020 records, and requested a status update on a crosswalk at Everett and Salem Streets.
